first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and two independent consolidated memories (31, 86) show durable, uncaveated evidence that simplifying onboarding lifts completion and downstream activation—this directly targets the current regression and supports sustainable qualified revenue rather than a reactive price war. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor entry pricing, but its own record flags a pooled-cohort confound from a mid-test redefinition, so it's verified rather than acted on this cycle; racing to match competitor pricing risks attracting low-quality, price-sensitive accounts that erode long-term revenue quality. I'm verifying memory_86 to confirm the onboarding effect still holds given the current regression (it may have eroded or interacted with other changes), and verifying memory_73 to check whether its caveat rules it out entirely or just weakens confidence, since it's the most consequential inherited memory intersecting with the acute competitive threat. Only one experiment slot is available, so I'm prioritizing the intervention with the cleanest evidentiary support and clearest link to the current KPI regression, while explicitly flagging the pricing risk for future consideration rather than silently ignoring the competitive threat.
